mainTopic: The כלל that a חטאת requires שגגה from beginning to end in throwing and carrying, and how intention makes an unusual spot count as a place
overview: The משנה teaches that someone who throws on שבת by mistake is פטור if he remembers mid-flight, or if the object is caught or burned before landing. It then states a כלל: a חטאת is brought only when both the beginning and the end of the act were בשגגה. The גמרא asks why the opening case implies that he is חייב if the object lands, when he already remembered. רב כהנא and רבא try several answers. רבא finally reads the opening line as two separate exempt cases. רב אשי instead fills in missing words: if the object lands, he is חייב only if he forgot again before it landed. Next, רבה and רבא discuss a case of two אמות שוגג, two מזיד, and two שוגג. The גמרא shows that רבה is speaking of carrying and רבא of throwing, so they do not really disagree. Finally, רבה rules that throwing on purpose into a dog's mouth or a furnace makes one חייב, because his intention makes it count as a place. רב ביבי בר אביי supports this from carrying food out in one's mouth, and the chapter ends.

steps.title: The thrower who remembers mid-flight, or whose object is caught or burned
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a thrower is פטור if he remembered after the object left his hand and it was then caught by a person or a dog, or it burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone throws, and remembers after it left his hand. If another person caught it, a dog caught it, or it burned, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a case of throwing on שבת without realizing it was forbidden. Something stops the throw from finishing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Throwing from one domain to another only counts as a מלאכה once the object lands and comes to rest. Here the object was caught or destroyed in the air, and the thrower also remembered mid-flight. Either way, no complete act was done בשגגה, so he does not bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: And he remembered (that it is שבת or that it is forbidden)

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who throws,
and remembered after it left his hand,
if another person caught it,
a dog caught it, or it was burned —
he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַזּוֹרֵק, וְנִזְכַּר מֵאַחַר שֶׁיָּצְתָה מִיָּדוֹ
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thrower who remembers mid-flight, and whose object is caught or burned before landing, is פטור from a חטאת.

steps.title: Throwing to wound, remembering before the wound happens
steps.stepSummary: Someone who throws in order to make a חבורה and remembers before the wound is made is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he threw something to wound a person or an animal, and remembered before the wound was made, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. This time the forbidden act is wounding, not carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a wound on שבת can be a מלאכה. The wound itself is the end of the act. He remembered before that end arrived, so the act was not completely בשגגה, and he is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A wound (which draws blood or bruises)

phrases.english: If he threw to make a wound,
whether on a person or on an animal,
and remembered before the wound was made —
he is exempt.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Remembering before the wound is made exempts the thrower.

steps.title: The general rule: beginning and end must both be unwitting
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states the כלל: a person is only חייב חטאת when both the beginning and the end of his act were בשגגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: everyone who is liable for a sin-offering is only liable if the beginning and end were unwitting. If the beginning was unwitting and the end deliberate, or the beginning deliberate and the end unwitting, they are exempt, until both beginning and end are unwitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the earlier cases with one general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת atones for a mistake. So the entire act, from start to finish, must be a mistake. If he knew at any stage, whether at the start or by the end, there is no חטאת.
steps.whatToRemember: A חטאת requires שגגה at both the start and the finish of the act.

phrases.english: This is the rule:
all who are liable for sin-offerings —
are not liable unless
their beginning and end are unwitting.
If the beginning was unwitting and the end deliberate,
or the beginning deliberate and the end unwitting —
they are exempt,
until both their beginning and end are unwitting.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for a חטאת requires שגגה from beginning to end.

steps.title: If the object lands, is he liable even though he remembered?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers from the first case that he is חייב if the object lands. That contradicts the כלל, because he remembered mid-flight.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: This implies that if it landed, he is liable. But he remembered! And we learned that one is only liable for a sin-offering if the beginning and end were unwitting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the first case closely and finds a contradiction with the general rule at the end of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts him only when the object was caught or burned. That suggests that if it simply landed, he would be חייב. But he remembered after throwing, so the end of his act was זדון. By the סיפא's rule, he should be פטור anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: But if it came to rest (landed)

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה never says 'if it landed he is חייב.' That is the גמרא's inference from the fact that only catching or burning was listed as exempting.

phrases.english: GEMARA: This implies that if it landed, he is liable?
But he remembered,
and we learned: all who are liable for sin-offerings
are not liable unless
their beginning and end are unwitting?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the רישא against the סיפא's כלל
steps.kashyaTarget: The implied liability in the רישא when the object lands
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Remembering mid-flight makes the end זדון, so by the כלל he should be פטור even if the object lands.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the rule refers to a bolt on a cord
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers that the סיפא's כלל speaks of an object tied to a cord, which the thrower can still pull back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: The latter clause refers to a bolt and a cord.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא resolves the contradiction by limiting the כלל to a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a cord, the thrower can still stop the act after remembering. So his end is truly זדון, and he is פטור. In an ordinary throw, nothing can be done once the object leaves his hand. The whole act therefore still counts as שגגה, and he is חייב if it lands.

keyTerms.meaning: We have come to (we are dealing with)
A bolt (peg) and a cord tied to it

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
In the latter clause we are dealing with a bolt and a cord.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: סֵיפָא אֲתָאן לְלַכְתָּא וּמִתְנָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the סיפא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כלל applies to every throw, so a thrower who remembers mid-flight would always be פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כלל applies where the act can still be reversed, as with a cord. An ordinary throw cannot be reversed, so it stays שגגה.

steps.title: A bolt on a cord is still held in his hand
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a tied object is still connected to the thrower, so no throw ever happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: A bolt and cord — he is holding it in his hand!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב כהנא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he still holds the cord, the object never fully left his possession. That is not a throw at all, so there was never a question of liability to discuss.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds it bound in his hand

phrases.english: A bolt and a cord —
he is holding it tied in his hand!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An object still tied to the thrower's hand has not been thrown, so it cannot create liability for throwing on שבת.

steps.title: The cord case is about wounding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the cord case refers to someone who meant to make a חבורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he intended to inflict a wound.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב כהנא by moving the cord case from carrying to wounding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For wounding, it does not matter whether the object is still tied to him. Only the wound matters. With a cord he can still pull back and prevent the wound, so remembering makes the end זדון.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; it is a case where

phrases.english: It is a case where he intended
to make a wound.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-defining the case (wounding rather than carrying)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The cord case was about carrying, so the cord ruins it as a throw.
steps.terutzMaskana: The cord case is about wounding, where the cord does not matter.

steps.title: The wounding case is already in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the משנה already explicitly taught the wounding case, so the כלל would add nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this: one who throws to make a wound, on a person or an animal, and remembered before the wound was made, is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the wounding explanation because it makes the כלל repetitive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said that remembering before the wound exempts him. Reading the כלל as being about wounding would just repeat that case. So the explanation fails.

phrases.english: This too we have already learned:
one who throws to make a wound,
whether on a person or on an animal,
and remembered before the wound was made —
is exempt!

steps.kashyaTarget: The wounding explanation of the כלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It makes the כלל a repetition of a case the משנה already stated.

steps.title: רבא: the rule refers to carrying
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests instead that the כלל refers to carrying an object while walking, not throwing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It refers to one who carries.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the cord approach and offers a new explanation of the כלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person carrying an object holds it the whole time, so he can stop the moment he remembers. That makes his end זדון, and the כלל exempts him. An ordinary throw still cannot be stopped, so the thrower would be חייב when the object lands.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries (walks the object across)

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It refers to one who carries.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The כלל must refer to a tied throw or to wounding.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כלל refers to carrying, where he can stop at any moment.

steps.title: But the rule is taught about throwing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the כלל comes in a משנה about throwing, so it cannot be limited to carrying.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the 'this is the rule' that was taught is taught about throwing!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects רבא's first explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole משנה deals with זריקה. A general rule stated at its end should cover its own topic, not shift to carrying. So the contradiction from step 4 is back.

phrases.english: But the 'this is the rule' that was taught,
was taught about throwing.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כלל sits in a משנה about throwing, so it must apply to throwing.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה teaches two separate exempt cases
steps.stepSummary: רבא re-reads the רישא as two separate cases. Remembering after the throw is enough to exempt him. And even if he did not remember, interception exempts him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: Two things are taught. One who throws and remembered after it left his hand is exempt. Alternatively, if he did not remember, but another person caught it, a dog caught it, or it burned, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his final answer. He changes how we read the first line of the משנה, so it no longer contradicts the כלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Remembering mid-flight already exempts him, even if the object lands, exactly as the כלל says. Catching or burning is a separate case, where he never remembered but the throw was never completed. The inference 'if it landed he is חייב' disappears, and the כלל applies to throwing as written.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא's conclusion, a thrower who remembers mid-flight is פטור even if the object lands. Catching or burning is a separate exemption for someone who never remembered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the כלל of תחילתו וסופו שגגה intact for throwing. Awareness gained at any point before the act is complete removes the חטאת, even when the act can no longer be stopped.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said,
two things are taught:
one who throws and remembered
after it left his hand,
or alternatively, he did not remember
and another person caught it
or a dog caught it, or it was burned —
he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's carrying answer after it was rejected
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the רישא as two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רישא was one case requiring both remembering and interception, which implied liability if the object landed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each half exempts on its own: remembering alone, or interception alone.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is no contradiction. Remembering mid-flight exempts him, and so does interception without remembering.

steps.title: רב אשי says the משנה is missing words and rebuilds the throwing case
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a new reading of the רישא. Remembering after the throw exempts him only if the object is intercepted (caught or burned). If the object lands, he is liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: the משנה is missing words. This is what it teaches: if someone throws and remembers after the object left his hand, and then another person caught it, or a dog caught it, or it was burned, he is exempt. But if it landed, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a different solution from רבא's. He says some words are missing from the משנה, and he fills them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא read the רישא as two separate reasons to be exempt: remembering alone, or interception alone. רב אשי joins them into one case: he remembered, and the object was also intercepted. So remembering by itself is not enough. If the object lands, the default is liability, and the next step adds a condition to that.

keyTerms.meaning: The text is missing words. The גמרא fills in what the משנה really means.
And this is what it teaches. Introduces the corrected reading.
Caught it (intercepted it in the air).

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב אשי with רבא from step 11. רבא said remembering alone exempts. רב אשי says remembering exempts only together with interception, or if he never forgot again (see the next step).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
The Mishnah is missing words,
and this is what it teaches:
One who throws and remembers
phrases.notes: He remembers either that it is שבת or that throwing is forbidden.

phrases.english: after it left his hand,
and another person caught it, or a dog caught it,
or it was burned, he is exempt.
But if it landed, he is liable.
phrases.notes: This is an inference from the משנה's wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: חַסּוֹרֵי מְחַסְּרָא, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer from רבא's in step 11 to the original difficulty of step 4: the רישא implies liability when the object lands, yet the כלל requires the end to be שגגה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Textual emendation (חסורי מחסרא). The two clauses of the רישא are combined into one case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Following רבא, remembering after the throw would exempt him all by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: Remembering plus interception exempts him. If the object lands, he is liable in the basic case, with a condition added next.

steps.title: Liability only if he forgot again, so the כלל has a job
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי continues. The liability when the object lands applies only if he forgot again before it landed. If he stayed aware, he is exempt, because a חטאת requires both the beginning and the end to be שגגה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When was it said that he is liable if the object lands? When he forgot again before it landed. But if he did not forget again, he is exempt. This is because everyone who brings a חטאת is liable only if the beginning and the end of the act were both done by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his reading of the משנה. He limits the liability for a landed object to a case where the thrower forgot again, so the רישא no longer contradicts the כלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The landing completes the מלאכה, so his state of mind at the landing matters. If he forgot again, the end of the act is שגגה, just like the beginning, so he brings a חטאת. If he stayed aware until it landed, the end was not שגגה, so he is exempt, exactly as the כלל says. The inference 'if it landed he is חייב' now applies only to one who forgot again, so it no longer contradicts the כלל.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? This limits the ruling just stated.
He went back and forgot again.
Their beginning and end are by mistake. This is the condition for bringing a חטאת.
Those who are obligated to bring sin-offerings.

steps.whatToRemember: In רב אשי's reading there are three outcomes. Remembered and intercepted: פטור. Landed after he forgot again: חייב. Landed while he stayed aware: פטור, because of the כלל of תחילתן וסופן שגגה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This resolves the opening contradiction of step 4 without re-reading the רישא as two cases (unlike רבא). The implied liability when the object lands is limited to one who forgot again before it landed.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
Where he then forgot again,
phrases.notes: He forgot again before the object landed.

phrases.english: but if he did not forget again, he is exempt,
because all who are liable for sin-offerings
are not liable unless
their beginning and their end are unwitting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב אשי's reconstruction. It limits the liability in the landing case and connects the כלל to it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the inferred liability (במה דברים אמורים) to a case where he forgot again, so that it fits the כלל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The inference 'if it landed he is חייב' seemed to apply even when he remembered mid-flight, which contradicts the כלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כלל teaches that if the end of the act is not שגגה, he is exempt even though it began as שגגה.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both the start and the completion of a מלאכה must be שגגה to bring a חטאת.

steps.title: A dispute: mistaken, deliberate, then mistaken carrying
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the כלל and brings a מחלוקת. Someone carries two אמות by mistake, two on purpose, and two by mistake again. רבה says פטור. רבא says חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: "This is the rule: all who are liable for חטאות..." It was stated: two אמות by mistake, two אמות on purpose, two אמות by mistake. רבה said: exempt. רבא said: liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic based on the כלל. It brings a case where the middle of the act is deliberate but the beginning and end are mistaken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כלל asks whether the beginning and the end are שגגה. Here they both are, but the middle section is מזיד. רבה exempts him and רבא obligates him. The next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: This is the rule. The words of the משנה being discussed.
It was stated. Introduces a dispute between אמוראים.
Two cubits. Carrying four אמות in רשות הרבים is the measure for liability.

phrases.aramaic: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי חַטָּאוֹת כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: "This is the rule: All who are liable for sin-offerings, etc."
It was stated:
Two cubits unwittingly,
phrases.notes: He is carrying in רשות הרבים.

phrases.english: two cubits intentionally,
two cubits unwittingly,
Rabba said: He is exempt.
Rava said: He is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה הַכְּלָל: כׇּל חַיָּיבֵי חַטָּאוֹת. אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from reading the משנה to a new case that tests the כלל of תחילתן וסופן שגגה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a case of 2 אמות שוגג, 2 מזיד, 2 שוגג: רבה rules פטור and רבא rules חייב.
steps.confusionAlert: רַבָּה and רָבָא are two different אמוראים with very similar names. Watch the spelling and vowels.

steps.title: Why רבה exempts, even according to רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: רבה exempts even according to רבן גמליאל, who holds that awareness during half a measure does not split the act. In רבן גמליאל's case the measure was completed by mistake. Here the four אמות were completed on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said he is exempt, even according to רבן גמליאל, who said that awareness in the middle of half a measure does not count. That applies there, because when the measure was completed, it was completed by mistake. But here it was completed on purpose, so no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבה's view. It shows that רבה's ruling fits even the opinion that seems most likely to disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל holds that becoming aware in the middle of half a measure does not separate the two halves, so he is still liable. רבה says that only works when the full measure is completed בשוגג. In our case, the first 2 אמות were שוגג and the next 2 were מזיד, so the four אמות of liability were completed on purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose view about awareness during a half-measure is being cited.
Awareness during half a measure does not count to divide the act.
He completed the measure that makes him liable.
There / here. Used to contrast two cases.

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the key question for רבה: what was his state of mind when the measure of liability was completed?

phrases.english: Rabba said he is exempt,
even according to Rabban Gamliel,
who said there is no awareness for half a measure,
phrases.notes: For example, someone eats half an olive-sized amount, becomes aware, forgets, and eats another half. He is still liable.

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם הוּא דְּכִי קָא גָמַר שִׁיעוּרָא —
phrases.english: that is only there, where when he completed the measure,
he completed it unwittingly,
but here, where he completed it intentionally, no.
phrases.notes: The four אמות were completed during the deliberate section.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּה אָמַר פָּטוּר, אֲפִילּוּ לְרַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבה's ruling from step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability depends on whether the measure was completed בשוגג. Here the four אמות were completed במזיד, so he is פטור even according to רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: What kind of case is this, throwing or carrying?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what action the dispute is about. It cannot be throwing, because a thrown object is all שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in what case? If it is about throwing, it is unwitting!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which kind of act the dispute between רבה and רבא is about. It first rules out throwing, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an object is thrown, the person cannot stop it. So even if he becomes aware mid-flight, he has done nothing on purpose. A middle section that is truly מזיד is only possible when the person himself keeps acting.

keyTerms.meaning: And in what case? Asks for the exact setting.

phrases.english: And in what case?
If with throwing, it is all unwitting!
phrases.notes: He cannot do anything to stop the object once it is in the air.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact setting of the dispute that was just explained.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute about throwing or carrying?

steps.title: The case is carrying
steps.stepSummary: The dispute must be about carrying (מעביר), where the person actively walks during the deliberate section.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about carrying.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question: the case is a person walking while carrying the object.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When someone carries, every step is his own new action. So the middle 2 אמות can truly be done on purpose. This is what makes the case of שוגג, מזיד, שוגג possible.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries an object while walking in רשות הרבים.

steps.whatToRemember: The dispute between רבה and רבא is about carrying four אמות, where the middle section was deliberate. For רבה, what matters is that the four אמות were completed במזיד.

phrases.english: Rather, it is with carrying.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The case is carrying (מעביר), where the deliberate middle section is truly the person's own action.

steps.title: רבא: Liable, Because a Thrown Object Is Out of His Control
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules חייב. He holds this even according to the רבנן, who say that awareness during half a measure splits the act. Their rule only applies when the action is still in the person's control.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: He is liable. This is true even according to the רבנן, who say that awareness during half a measure counts. They only say that there, where the action is in his hands. But here, where it is not in his hands, they would not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: Now we hear רבא's side of the מחלוקת. He says the person is חייב, and he explains why even the רבנן, whose view (יש ידיעה לחצי שיעור) usually leads to exemption, would agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן hold that becoming aware in the middle of a measure splits the act into two halves, and each half is too small to be חייב. רבא limits this to cases where the person can still stop what he is doing. If the person has no control during the aware part, his awareness does not split anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Awareness in the middle of a measure, which can split one act into two halves
In his hands, meaning under his control
The Sages, here the side arguing against רבן גמליאל

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה, who exempts, with רבא, who obligates. Their names are almost the same in Hebrew.

phrases.english: Rava said: He is liable,
and even according to the Rabbis who say
there is awareness for half a measure,
that is only there, where it is in his control,
phrases.notes: In the רבנן's case he can still stop.

phrases.english: but here, where it is not in his control, not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבה's exemption from Step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Awareness in the middle does not split the act when the person has no control over it, so he is חייב.

steps.title: Which Action Is רבא Talking About?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what case רבא means. It cannot be carrying, because when someone carries, the object stays in his control.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in what case? If it is carrying, the object is in his hands!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about רבא that it asked about רבה: what action is he discussing? It rules out carrying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's reason is that the person had no control. A person who carries can stop walking at any time, so carrying does not fit his reason. That leaves only one option.

keyTerms.meaning: One who carries an object while walking

phrases.english: And in what case?
If with carrying, it is in his control!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which case fits רבא's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבא is talking about carrying or throwing.

steps.title: רבא Is Talking About Throwing
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that רבא must be talking about throwing. So רבה (carrying) and רבא (throwing) do not really disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is about throwing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא must mean a throw. This closes the discussion of רבה and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once an object leaves the thrower's hand, he cannot stop it, so his awareness changes nothing. This shows the two אמוראים are ruling on different cases, not arguing.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה exempts in carrying, because the middle part was done on purpose while he was in control. רבא obligates in throwing, because the object was out of his control. They do not actually disagree.

phrases.english: Rather, with throwing.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא's ruling is about throwing, where the object is out of the person's control.

steps.title: רבה: Throwing Into a Dog's Mouth or a Furnace Is Liable
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that if someone throws an object and it lands in a dog's mouth or in a furnace, he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: If he threw it and it came to rest in a dog's mouth or in a furnace, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבה gives a ruling about where a thrown object lands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For throwing to count as a מלאכה, the object must come to rest (הנחה) in a proper place. רבה says a dog's mouth or a furnace still counts as a resting place, even though the object is eaten or burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Came to rest, meaning it landed

phrases.english: Rabba said:
If he threw and it came to rest in the mouth of a dog
or in the mouth of a furnace, he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: זָרַק וְנָחָה בְּפִי הַכֶּלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about where a thrown object lands.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thrown object that lands in a dog's mouth or a furnace makes the thrower חייב.

steps.title: Challenge From the משנה: A Dog Catching It Exempts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבה from a משנה. It says that if a dog caught the object, or it was burned, the thrower is פטור.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned: If someone else caught it, or a dog caught it, or it was burned, he is exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה's ruling with a משנה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה exempts the thrower when a dog catches the object or it gets burned. That sounds exactly like רבה's case, where he said חייב. So there seems to be a contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn? (introduces a challenge from a משנה)

phrases.english: But didn't we learn:
If another caught it, or a dog caught it,
or it was burned, he is exempt!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's ruling that landing in a dog's mouth or a furnace makes the thrower חייב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה exempts in what looks like the same case.

steps.title: The Difference Is Intention
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is about someone who did not plan for the dog to catch it. רבה is talking about someone who aimed for the dog's mouth.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, he did not intend it. Here, he did intend it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing the two cases are different. What matters is what the thrower was aiming for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the dog snatched the object on the way, so the thrower's plan was cut off. In רבה's case, the thrower aimed at the dog's mouth, so his plan was carried out. That is why he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: There / here, used to contrast two cases

steps.confusionAlert: The dog's mouth is the same in both cases. The only difference is whether the thrower aimed for it.

phrases.english: There, where he did not intend it;
here, where he does intend it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק) based on intention
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A dog's mouth or a fire can never count as a resting place.
steps.terutzMaskana: If the thrower aimed for it, the dog's mouth counts as a resting place and he is חייב.

steps.title: רב ביבי בר אביי Begins a Proof: One Act of Eating, Many Offerings
steps.stepSummary: רב ביבי בר אביי says a משנה supports רבה's idea. He first quotes a case where one act of eating brings four חטאות and one אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ביבי בר אביי said: We also learned this. There is a person who eats once and is liable for four sin-offerings and one guilt-offering: an impure person who ate forbidden fat that was נותר from holy offerings, on יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ביבי בר אביי starts bringing a support for the idea that intention counts. This step only sets up the source. The proof itself comes in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists one act of eating that breaks many prohibitions at once: eating holy food while impure, חלב, נותר, and eating on יום הכפורים. Each one needs its own חטאת. The אשם is for using holy property (מעילה). The key part for the proof is רבי מאיר's addition that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned it (introduces a supporting source)
Leftover sacrificial meat whose time to be eaten has passed

phrases.english: Rav Beivai bar Abaye said:
We too have also learned:
There is one who eats one act of eating

phrases.aramaic: וְחַיָּיב עָלֶיהָ אַרְבַּע חַטָּאוֹת וְאָשָׁם אֶחָד.
phrases.english: and is liable for it four sin-offerings and one guilt-offering.
An impure person who ate forbidden fat,
and it was leftover from consecrated offerings,
on Yom Kippur.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a proof for the intention-based answer of Step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That intention can make an unusual spot count as a place.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כריתות about one act of eating that brings many offerings.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: Carrying Food Out in His Mouth on שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר adds that if it was שבת and he carried the food out in his mouth, he is חייב one more חטאת. The חכמים answer that this is a different kind of sin, but they do not deny that he is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Also, if it was שבת and he carried it out in his mouth, he is liable. They said to him: That is not of the same type.
steps.whatsHappening: This continues the quote of the משנה. It brings the part that רב ביבי needs: carrying out with the mouth on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר counts a fifth חטאת for carrying on שבת. The חכמים only object that carrying is a different kind of sin from eating, so it does not belong on a list about eating. Both sides still agree that he is חייב for carrying in his mouth.

keyTerms.meaning: He carried it out in his mouth
It is not of the same category (it is not an eating sin)

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying he is פטור. They agree he is חייב. They only object to counting it on this list.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir says:
Also, if it was Shabbat
and he carried it out in his mouth, he is liable.
They said to him: It is not of the same type.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: אַף אִם הָיְתָה שַׁבָּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quoted משנה with the part the proof depends on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying food out in one's mouth on שבת makes a person חייב.

steps.title: Why Liable? The Mouth Is Not the Normal Way to Carry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why he is חייב at all. People do not normally carry things in their mouths.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why? That is not the normal way of carrying out!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp question about the משנה. The answer to this question is what will prove רבה's point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, a מלאכה done in an unusual way does not make a person חייב. Carrying in the mouth is unusual. So something must explain why he is still חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not the normal way of carrying out

phrases.english: And why?
This is not the normal way of carrying out!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? הָא אֵין דֶּרֶךְ הוֹצָאָה בְּכָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason behind the ruling in Step 25 in order to draw out the proof.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why carrying in the mouth counts, even though it is not the normal way.

steps.title: His Intention Makes It Count as a Place, in Both Cases
steps.stepSummary: Because he meant to carry it in his mouth, his intention makes his mouth count as a place. In the same way, the thrower's intention makes the dog's mouth count as a place. This supports רבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since he intends it, his thought makes it a place. Here too, since he intends it, his thought makes it a place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question and finishes רב ביבי's proof. Intention turns the mouth into a real place, and the same is true for the dog's mouth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mouth is not normally a place for holding objects, but a person's plan can make it one. רב ביבי applies this to רבה's case. When the thrower aims for the dog's mouth, his intention makes it a valid resting place, so he is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: Here too (applies the idea to the case at hand)

steps.whatToRemember: A person's intention can turn an unusual spot, like his own mouth or a dog's mouth, into a valid place for a שבת מלאכה. That is why רבה makes the thrower חייב when he aims for the dog's mouth.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a general principle in הלכות שבת: מחשבה can give a spot the status of a מקום, even if it is not normally used that way.

phrases.english: Rather: since he intends it,
his thought makes it a place.
Here too, since he intends it,
his thought makes it a place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 26 and uses the answer to support רבה from Steps 21 and 23.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's ruling that aiming at a dog's mouth makes the thrower חייב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי מאיר's case of carrying in the mouth, which works only because of intention.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Intention can make an unusual spot count as a place, so throwing into a dog's mouth on purpose makes the thrower חייב.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the Chapter of Throwing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא formally closes פרק הזורק with the traditional הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, chapter 'One Who Throws.'
steps.whatsHappening: There is no new argument here. The גמרא is simply marking the end of the chapter called הזורק with the traditional closing line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן means 'we will return.' It expresses the learner's wish to come back to this chapter and keep reviewing it. The chapter is named for its first word, הזורק. That opening משנה is about one who throws an object from רשות היחיד to רשות הרבים on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. The traditional formula said when finishing a chapter.
One who throws. This is the name of the chapter, taken from its opening word.
A chapter of the משנה and גמרא.

steps.whatToRemember: The chapter ends on the idea from the last sugya: מחשבתו משויא ליה מקום. A person's intention can make an unusual spot, such as a dog's mouth or his own mouth, count as a real resting place for the מלאכה.
steps.confusionAlert: The הדרן is not part of the halachic discussion. It is not a ruling or a proof. It is only a closing line for the chapter.

phrases.english: We will return to you, [the chapter of] 'One Who Throws'
phrases.notes: Traditional closing formula. The chapter name comes from the first word of its opening משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comes right after the final proof for רבה's view in Step 27, and closes the whole chapter.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק הזורק is complete. The learner commits to return and review it.
